title: Persist investigation output to the repo and link it to the planning node
description:
The jit-planning-lead dispatch-hygiene rule sends sub-agent output to session scratch files, and the investigator prompt inherits that default. The plan-review gate, however, checks that sources the plan cites as authoritative are repo-resident and linked to the planning node. During the 2821e177 run these two rules collided: the plan cited the investigation report by its scratchpad path, the gate flagged the citation as an unavailable source, and the report had to be copied into `dev/active/` and re-cited mid-round, costing part of a review cycle.

Fix the skill so the two rules compose: `.claude/skills/jit-planning-lead/SKILL.md` (Step 4b) directs the investigator to write its findings report to a repo path derived from the container (for example `dev/active/{container.short_id}-investigation.md`), and the lead links it to the planning node with `jit doc add` alongside the plan. Scratch files stay the default for intermediate artifacts that no reviewed document cites; anything the plan will cite as grounding is repo-resident from the start. The skill success criterion "all the planning artifacts are linked to the corresponding JIT issues" then holds by construction.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: the Step 4b investigator dispatch in jit-planning-lead names a repo-resident output path under the managed active-docs directory, derived from the container id.
- [hard] REQ-02: Step 4b instructs the lead to link the investigation report to the planning node with `jit doc add` before the plan-review gate runs.
- [hard] REQ-03: the dispatch-hygiene section distinguishes cited grounding artifacts (repo-resident, linked) from intermediate scratch output (session scratchpad), stating the rule for each.
